questions.explain: The gate: baseline CPU below 40% → accept compression if post-compression CPU stays below 55%; 40–60% → row compression only, reject page if the delta exceeds 8 percentage points; above 60% → do not apply page compression at all. The chapter's worked example: 15% CPU increase on an 8-vCore Business Critical instance ($1.008/hr) costs ~$108/month while 800 GB of storage savings is $92/month — a net loss, so the tradeoff must be weighed.

questions.explain: Backup savings compound primary savings: RDS has no direct compress-backups toggle — a smaller primary volume produces smaller block-level snapshots; exports to S3 via Parquet get Snappy compression automatically (~$0.023/GB-month S3 vs $0.095 snapshot storage). Azure SQL compresses backups automatically, so table compression multiplies with backup compression (50% + 30% ≈ 65% smaller).
